description: First contact with programming: thinking in algorithms, writing them as pseudocode and flowcharts, then as real code with variables, control flow, functions and a first look at objects. Taught to the depth of a leading first programming course, with a working program every week.
modelledOn: Zelle, Python Programming: An Introduction to Computer Science
Guttag, Introduction to Computation and Programming
Roberts, The Art and Science of Java
outcomes: Explain how source code becomes a running program and the roles of compilers, interpreters and linkers.
Design an algorithm for a stated problem and express it as pseudocode and a flowchart before coding.
Write programs that use variables, expressions, selection and loops correctly, and trace them by hand.
Decompose a program into functions with clear parameters and return values.
Explain objects, classes, attributes and methods and use simple objects in a program.
Find and fix syntax, runtime and logic errors with a systematic debugging method and tests.

units.title: Programs, languages and translators
topics: What a program is; machine code, low-level and high-level languages; why there are many languages
Compilers, interpreters, assemblers and linkers; the edit-run-debug loop
Setting up an editor and running a first program; printing and reading input
Programming vocabulary: source, syntax, semantics, statement, expression, bug

units.title: Algorithms, pseudocode and flowcharts
topics: Properties of an algorithm: finite, definite, effective; inputs and outputs
Pseudocode conventions; flowchart symbols for process, decision, loop, input/output
Tracing an algorithm with a trace table
Everyday algorithms: making change in cedis, computing a GPA, finding the largest of three numbers
From flowchart to code and back

units.title: Data: character set, constants, types, variables
topics: Character set, identifiers, keywords and naming rules
Literals and constants; integer, floating-point, character, string and boolean types
Variables, declaration, assignment and memory as named boxes
Type conversion and casting; integer division and rounding surprises
Input, output and formatting numbers and strings

units.title: Operators and expressions
topics: Arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment and increment operators
Precedence and associativity; evaluating expressions by hand
Boolean expressions and short-circuit evaluation
Common expression errors: off-by-one, mixing types, confusing = and ==

units.title: Selection
topics: if, if-else, else-if ladders and nested ifs
switch statements and when to prefer them
Designing conditions: grade bands, tax brackets, leap years
Testing every branch; boundary values

units.title: Iteration
topics: while, do-while and for loops; loop variable, condition, update
Counting, summing, averaging and finding maxima in a loop
Sentinel-controlled and flag-controlled loops; break and continue
Nested loops: multiplication tables, patterns, simple matrices
Infinite loops and termination; choosing the right loop

units.title: Functions and program structure
topics: Defining and calling functions; parameters, arguments, return values
Scope and lifetime of variables; local and global
Decomposition and stepwise refinement; top-down design
Library functions: maths, strings, random numbers
Introduction to recursion: factorial and Fibonacci

units.title: Collections and strings
topics: Arrays and lists: indexing, traversal, searching, finding min and max
Strings as sequences of characters; common string operations
Reading and writing a simple text file
Simple sorting by hand: bubble sort and selection sort

units.title: Basic object-oriented concepts
topics: Objects as data plus behaviour; classes as blueprints
Attributes and methods; creating and using objects
Encapsulation and why it matters; a Student or BankAccount class
Objects already met: strings, lists, files

units.title: Identifying and fixing errors
topics: Syntax, runtime and logic errors and how each shows itself
Reading error messages and stack traces
Debugging strategy: reproduce, isolate, hypothesise, test; print statements and a debugger
Writing test cases before and after fixing; defensive input checking
Code style, comments and documentation
